newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to sell diesel fuel from state reserves.
newsitem.headline: Poland to sell diesel fuel from state reserves.

text.p: The Polish government on Tuesday decided to start selling diesel fuel from state reserves to stabilise the gasoline market hit by high world oil prices, deputy Industry Minister Roman Czerwinski said.
"In the first move we plan to sell 120,000 tonnes of diesel fuel, which would help us survive...a period of high external prices," Czerwinski told reporters after a cabinet meeting.

He said about 30,000 tonnes of diesel would be sold each week during the next month. The first auction would be staged on Wednesday, at which 31,500 tonnes of diesel would be offered to large and small distributors.
During the auction, 20,000 tonnes of diesel would be offered in two tranches for large distributors and 11,500 tonnes in several tranches for smaller sellers.
Poland has seen diesel supplies temporarily drying up due to high world oil prices coupled with official caps on gasoline prices.
The government did not introduce duty-free import quotas of 300,000 tonnes of gasoline and of 400,000 tonnes of diesel as some analysts expected.
Government spokeswoman Aleskandra Jakubowska earlier said that any duty-free import quotas would probably be introduced along with the planned liberalisation of liquid fuel prices.
The liberalisation was originally planned for this year but Czerwinski declined to say when it would take place.

The finance ministry, which controls fuel prices, opposes their quick liberalisation, fearing it would jeopardise plans to reduce inflation to 17 percent in December this year from 21.6 percent in 1995.

But Polish refineries and distributors complain that world oil prices and official limits on price increases make production and imports increasingly less profitable and are pressing the government to allow prices to rise.

The Polish Liquid Fuels Chamber, a private distributors' group, which lobbies for duty-free quotas and price liberalisation, said some 300,000 tonnes of gasoline and 400,000 tonnes of diesel were needed to stabilise the market. -- Robert Bogdanski +48 22 653 9700
